old_caption: The video captures a small toy train navigating a winding track embedded in a sandy environment. The train, featuring a minifigure with a red hat, moves along the black plastic track, which is partially buried in the sand. The track curves gently to the right, forming a loop that the train follows. The sandy terrain around the track is uneven, with some areas appearing freshly disturbed. A wooden post stands prominently on the left side of the frame. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the train's journey along the track, capturing the dynamic interaction between the toy and its sandy surroundings.

The sandy terrain around the track is uneven, with some areas appearing freshly disturbed, possibly by the train's passage or other unseen activity. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the train's journey along the track, capturing the dynamic interaction between the toy and its sandy surroundings.
caption: The video captures a sandy, beach-like setting where a black plastic train track is laid in a winding S-curve across the grains. A weathered wooden post stands at the left edge and a small dark twig is stuck in the sand near the upper bend, both remaining fixed throughout. The track lies empty for the opening portion before a gray LEGO vehicle carrying a minifigure with a yellow head, red cap and red torso slides into view from the bottom-right corner. The vehicle then travels continuously along the rails, following the curve from the foreground toward the upper-middle of the scene. Its orientation turns with each bend of the track, and its apparent size steadily diminishes as it recedes into the distance. Slight motion blur accompanies the movement, while the sand, post and track stay in the same positions. The vehicle is still progressing along the far curve.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
